sections.section_name: Electrical (As Specifically Listed - NONE Listed - Flag)
sections.notes: Zero electrical confirmed by answer — no rough-in, no devices; the 6h/$95 carry has no component and should size to zero

flags.message: Proposal cover title 'Deck Building' and sole line item 'Build Deck as Above' describe no deck; the itemized scope is paver demo, slab, shed roof, screen enclosure, fireplace — deck component carries zero and the 'posts integrated with existing deck framing' language is a carry-over error superseded by the turned-down-footing answer.

Post count is now settled at 7-9 (carried 8) but the JBD prices 5 posts and zero turned-down footings — post material, footing excavation/forming, and ~0.5-0.7 cy extra concrete are all missing from the JBD concrete and framing sections, so its 42h/70h should not be read as covering them.

JBD carries $0 permits and no inspection line items while the answer confirms a Johnson City building permit with framing and fireplace/chimney inspections — permit_items and bundled_inspections receive no JBD hours but must not be zero downstream; inspection holds gate framing close and fireplace veneer.
JBD knee wall '~60 LF' vs settled 36 LF (two open sides, house on two sides); the 48h screen labor and $285/$345/$585 screen material lines are built on three sides and are overstated by roughly 40%.

JBD roof-structure labor includes 'chimney-penetration framing', TL 8h for 10-3-2 chimney-height work, and $245 chimney roof flashing/storm collar, but the settled location and termination put the chimney outside the shed roof edge ending just above the low eave — that work reduces to a chase-to-eave counterflash detail, not a penetration or a tall chase.

The chimney-termination policy (cap just above the ~8' low eave, not above the shed roof's high side) sits below the shed roof plane within 10' horizontally, which is the geometry 10-3-2 normally forbids — the confirmed fireplace/chimney inspection is where this could be rejected, so sizing should not assume the chase height is final until the inspector or the firebox manufacturer's termination table signs off.

Footprint: proposal ~12.5'×23.5' (294 sqft) vs drawing plan 22'-11"×11'-8" clear (267 sqft); knee wall 2' white vinyl (proposal) vs 3'-4 1/4" lap siding / ~3' beadboard (drawings); drawings add a screened transom band and painted brick chase not in the proposal or JBD — per canon the proposal governs and these stay logged, not adopted.

Roof structure 70h for a ~300 sqft single-plane shed roof with 19 rafters, two beams, ~8 posts and 10 sheets of sheathing runs hot; a 3-person crew would normally frame and sheathe this in 2-2.5 days (~50h), and with the ledger replaced by a beam on posts and the eave tie-in limited to gutter removal the only extra effort is post/beam setting.

WB fireplace structure 98h (90h GL) is heavy now that the manufactured firebox + Class A pipe in a ~6'-wide framed chase terminating at the low eave is settled — a manufactured kit is typically a 3-4 day, 2-person install (~50-65h); the 98h only made sense against the masonry option that is now off the table.
Screened enclosure 48h for ~33 LF of 2' knee wall, screen frames, one door and trim is on the high side (2-person crew ~3 days is the ceiling), and inherits the 60 LF overstatement above.
Electrical 6h and $95 material carried for a scope confirmed zero-electrical with no rough-in — this collapses to 0h; the JBD's own PM notes anticipated this.

General conditions 30h includes 18h PM for fireplace-system and finish-selection coordination that is now complete per answers (all selections final, lead times known) — remaining PM effort is scheduling, permit pull, and inspection coordination, closer to 8-12h.

No roof pitch or beam/post sizing exists in any source (sized in-house per IRC tables, not yet done); roof area is carried as plan area (~300 sqft) with no slope factor, and the exact chase/cap height is undimensioned even though termination is settled at 'just above the low eave'.

Firebox + Class A kit lead time is 3-4 weeks and the kit dimensions drive the fireplace footing thickening and chase framing — with the 'no demo without materials' policy, the kit (or at least its spec sheet) must be in hand before the slab pour, which the JBD's ~5-6 wk duration does not account for.

Concrete patio is mapped to groundwork (foundation before framing) rather than concrete_landscape because it now carries the fireplace footing and every post footing; downstream should expect no separate flatwork phase after the shell, and yard restoration is excluded by the JBD.

Fireplace structure split between structural_framing and rough_meps is a best-fit only — a Class A solid-fuel chimney system is not an MEP trade; the framed-chase answer at least keeps it in-house carpentry rather than a mason's scope.
